newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sun Direct wins 10000 contracts in first year.
newsitem.headline: Sun Direct wins 10000 contracts in first year.

text.p: Sun Direct, the German direct-selling subsidiary of the UK composit insurer Royal & Sun Alliance, gained 10,000 motor insurance customers and had an annual premium volume of 9.5 million marks in its first 13 months, marketing chief Hein Kuiper said on Friday.
The company started selling on a regional basis in October 1995 and in the whole of Germany in January 1996. By the end of the year, Sun Direct should have 14,000 contracts, Kuiper said.

Kuiper said the company was seeking to differentiate more than other German insurers, and added that mileage, the age of the driver and the use of the car all played a role. Car owners who made sure that no-one under 25 could use the car could gain a rebate of up to 20 percent, he said.
From 1997 the company will also offer private accident and contents policies, and later a life company will be added.

Sun Direct has 104 staff operating 99 telephone lines in the Duesseldorf headquarters and plans to spemd some six million marks on advertising this year. The company said 14 to 16 of callers buy insurance.

Start-up costs are around 80 million marks, to be spent up to the year 2000, by which time the company should break even, Kuiper said. Sun Direct expects direct-selling insurance to increase its market share from three percent to between seven and ten percent by the year 2000. In the UK it is 28 percent now and should be 33 to 40 percent in four years, Kuiper said.
Germany was nevertheless a very important and lucrative market, said Mike Jones, head of group corporate affairs of Royal & Sun Alliance.

"The average premium for one car is about double in Germany than in the UK, more than 1,000 marks versus 500 marks," he said. The number of privately-owned cars was double that of the UK. Royal & Sun also believes that there is "enormous cross-selling potential", and that Germany is strategically important for the group's European market entry.

In addition to Sun Direct, Royal & Sun owns the Securitas group in Bremen. Jones would not rule out the acquisition of a further company, but said there were at present no projects. German companies were in any case too expensive, he said. -- Reuters Insurance News
